prompt.context: Your client is Royal Cinemas, a NYC theater chain. Their revenue has been badly hurt by decreasing ticket sales, which are at their lowest point since 1996 for both the chain and the industry at large. Royal Cinemas is interested in converting their theaters into luxury cinemas.
prompt.question: Should Royal Cinemas convert their theaters into luxury cinemas?

clarifying_info.q: What is the timeframe for entry if they decide to proceed?
clarifying_info.a: If they choose to enter the market, they intend to enter immediately.

clarifying_info.q: How does Royal Cinemas currently price tickets and concessions?
clarifying_info.a: Currently prices tickets and concessions the same as competitors.

clarifying_info.q: How many competitors are in the NYC luxury cinema market?
clarifying_info.a: There are fewer than 5 major players in NYC.
Revenue has been steadily declining for 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: How many locations does Royal Cinemas currently operate?
Has Royal Cinemas previously attempted to enter the luxury space?
clarifying_info.a: No, they have not previously attempted to enter the luxury space.

clarifying_info.q: Is there data on luxury market growth?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, that information will be shared after the interviewer sees how the candidate would like to approach the problem from a high level.

exhibits.title: U.S. Cinema Market Share Trends
exhibits.shows: A chart showing market share trends over time for standard vs. luxury cinema categories in the U.S.
exhibits.data: Luxury theaters gaining market share over time as standard theaters lose market share

exhibits.title: Royal Cinemas: Current State vs. Luxury State Financial Comparison
exhibits.shows: A side-by-side table comparing key operating metrics for Royal Cinemas under its current standard model versus a proposed luxury conversion

framework: Financial Implications: Costs (renovations, equipment, shutdown costs if unprofitable) and Revenues (ticket pricing, concession pricing, number of customers, break-even point)
Market Attractiveness: Size and growth of the luxury cinema market, consumer tastes and preferences, whether target consumers differ from current base
Competitive Analysis: Key players and their market share, differentiating factors, anticipated competitor response to Royal Cinemas entry

questions.prompt: Based on Exhibit 1 (luxury market share trends), what does this tell you about the attractiveness of the luxury cinema market?
questions.guidance: A good candidate identifies the general trend: luxury theaters are gaining market share as standard theaters lose share, signaling a promising opportunity. An excellent candidate quantifies the shift and notes that the U.S. data may not fully represent the NYC market specifically.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate the expected weekly revenue for Royal Cinemas under both the current standard state and the luxury state. How does this influence your recommendation?
questions.guidance: A good candidate correctly calculates expected revenue in both states and identifies that luxury revenue is meaningfully higher despite fewer seats per screen, driven by higher prices and higher actual capacity utilization. An excellent candidate notes qualitative nuances: current state benefits from brand familiarity but faces streaming competition; luxury state offers a better experience but capacity projections are assumptions not yet proven.

math.setup:
Potential Revenue/Week = # Locations x # Screens x # Seats x # Showings x (Ticket Price + Avg Concession Spend). Expected Revenue = Potential Revenue x Capacity %.

Current Standard State:
  Peak: 10 x 10 x 150 x 20 x $20 = $6,000,000 potential; x 80% = $4,800,000
  Off-Peak: 10 x 10 x 150 x 40 x $20 = $12,000,000 potential; x 20% = $2,400,000
  Total Standard Weekly Revenue = $7,200,000

Luxury State:
  Peak: 10 x 10 x 65 x 20 x $50 = $6,500,000 potential; x 90% = $5,850,000
  Off-Peak: 10 x 10 x 65 x 40 x $50 = $13,000,000 potential; x 30% = $3,900,000
  Total Luxury Weekly Revenue = $9,750,000
steps: Ticket Price + Avg Concession Spend/person: Standard = $10 + $10 = $20; Luxury = $15 + $35 = $50
Standard Peak potential: 10 x 10 x 150 x 20 x $20 = $6,000,000; expected: $6,000,000 x 80% = $4,800,000
Standard Off-Peak potential: 10 x 10 x 150 x 40 x $20 = $12,000,000; expected: $12,000,000 x 20% = $2,400,000
Luxury Off-Peak potential: 10 x 10 x 65 x 40 x $50 = $13,000,000; expected: $13,000,000 x 30% = $3,900,000
Luxury revenue exceeds standard revenue by $2,550,000 per week (~35% uplift) despite having fewer seats per screen
math.answer: Standard weekly revenue: $7,200,000. Luxury weekly revenue: $9,750,000. Luxury generates ~$2.55M more per week.

questions.prompt: Royal Cinemas would like to know how long it will take to recoup their conversion and renovation costs. Calculate the payback period.
questions.guidance: A good candidate correctly calculates the payback period using the provided renovation cost and the net weekly cash flow after variable costs. An excellent candidate flags that the payback period appears very short and questions whether the assumptions (especially capacity projections) are too optimistic, and may note that closed theaters during renovation represent additional revenue loss.

math.setup:
Payback Period = Initial Investment / Net Weekly Cash Flow
Initial investment: $100M
Projected luxury weekly revenue: $9.75M (from Exhibit 2 calculation)
Projected luxury weekly variable costs: 50% of weekly revenue = $9.75M x 50% = $4.875M (~$5M)
Net weekly cash flow = $9.75M - $4.875M = $4.875M (~$4.875M)
steps: Weekly variable costs = 50% of weekly revenue = 50% x $9.75M = $4.875M
math.answer: Payback period ≈ 20.5 weeks or approximately 5 months. Formula: $100M / ($9.75M x 0.5) = 20.51 weeks.

brainstorming.prompt: Royal Cinemas is aware that it will need to compete with other successful luxury cinemas in New York City. How might it differentiate itself in this space?

categories.name: Concessions
ideas: Partnership with a well-known food market, restaurant, or celebrity chef
In-theater waiter service (consider a food/drink minimum to capture concession revenue)

categories.name: Environment
ideas: Premium, comfortable seating (e.g., recliners, wider spacing)
Work cafe with wifi outside the theater to encourage dwell time and additional spending
Aromatherapy or scent design in the theater

categories.name: Added Content
ideas: Regular talk-backs with film crew or directors after screenings
Special film shorts or exclusive previews before each movie

categories.name: Partnerships & Other
ideas: Partnerships with luxury hotel chains or high-end gyms for cross-promotions
Loyalty or membership programs targeting affluent NYC consumers

recommendation: Royal Cinemas should proceed with the conversion to luxury cinemas. The luxury cinema market is projected to gain market share as standard theater attendance declines. The financial analysis shows luxury operations generate approximately $9.75M per week versus $7.2M currently, and the payback period on the $100M renovation investment is only approximately 5 months. There are also plentiful opportunities for differentiation in the NYC luxury space.
risks: Intense competition with existing NYC luxury cinema operators
Revenue loss from theaters closed during renovations
Capacity utilization projections are assumptions; if overestimated, the revenue upside will be overstated
Significant reliance on high concession spend per person — a minimum spend policy may be needed to protect revenue
Brand confusion if Royal Cinemas keeps some standard locations alongside luxury conversions
Continued threat from streaming services — if in-person attendance declines further, even the luxury format may not compensate
next_steps: Ensure organizational structure and staffing are ready for the luxury service model
Develop a marketing strategy to attract luxury consumers while retaining loyal existing customers
Evaluate cost-effective, on-brand partnership opportunities for concessions and amenities
